seg: the teacher — the one about to receive the credit
THE POINT — 'thanks to': the cause named, and the credit handed over with it
passed — the good outcome the credit is for
okage.note: おかげ is 御蔭 — honorable shade: the good thing happened standing in someone's shade. Good outcomes only; when the outcome is bad the language reaches for せいで.

wr.t: おかげで can be aimed ironically at a bad outcome — 君のおかげでひどい目にあった — but only when the speaker wants the sting heard. The irony works because the word's home is gratitude.
wr.jp: 君のおかげで、ひどい目にあったよ。
wr.en: Thanks a lot to you, I had an awful time.

items.q: 先生の___、合格しました。
items.en: Thanks to my teacher, I passed.
items.why: Good outcome, credit handed to the teacher → おかげで.

items.q: 早く出た___、間に合いました。
items.en: Because I left early — and I'm glad I did — I made it.
items.why: The outcome is good and the early start gets the credit.

items.q: 雨の___、試合が中止になりました。
items.en: The match was called off because of the rain — and the rain gets the blame.
items.why: Bad outcome, cause blamed → せいで, not おかげで.

items.q: ___、元気です。
items.en: Thanks for asking — I'm well. (the fixed courtesy)
items.why: おかげさまで — the set phrase: credit to everything and everyone, politely.

items.q: 薬の___、よく眠れました。
items.en: Thanks to the medicine, I slept well.
items.why: Slept well = good outcome → the medicine gets おかげで.

seg: the rain — about to take the fault
THE POINT — 'because of', with the blame attached
was called off — the bad outcome
seide.note: せい points a finger: the cause is named AND blamed, and what follows is bad. おかげで's exact mirror — the sentence cannot stay neutral once either is in it.

wr.t: せいにする turns the blaming into a verb: to pin something on someone. 人のせいにする — to blame others — is where this word does its most social work.
wr.jp: 失敗を人のせいにしないでください。
wr.en: Don't pin the failure on other people.

items.q: 雨の___、試合が中止になりました。
items.en: The match was called off because of the rain.
items.why: Bad outcome, cause blamed → せいで.

items.q: 寝坊した___、遅刻しました。
items.en: I was late because I overslept.
items.why: The oversleeping takes the fault for a bad result.

items.q: 先生の___、合格しました。
items.en: Thanks to my teacher, I passed.
items.why: Good outcome → credit, not blame.

items.q: これは誰の___ですか。
items.en: Whose fault is this?
items.why: せい is the noun of fault itself.

items.q: 失敗を人の___にしないでください。
items.en: Don't pin the failure on other people.
items.why: せいにする — to make it someone's fault.

seg: one word — the single small thing
THE POINT — 'just because': one small cause, one outsized bad result, and the regret that it was avoidable
bakarini.note: The narrow, emotional member of the blame family: the cause must be SMALL and the bad result LARGE, and the sentence carries the regret that the small thing could so easily have gone the other way.

wr.t: If the cause was big or the result mild, ばかりに rings false — せいで is the honest marker there. ばかりに is reserved for the tiny hinge the disaster turned on.
wr.jp: 安いチケットを買ったばかりに、ひどい席になりました。
wr.en: Just because I bought the cheap ticket, I ended up with an awful seat.

items.q: 一言言わなかった___、大きな問題になりました。
items.en: Just because I didn't say one word, it turned into a real problem.
items.why: Tiny omission, big bad result, regret → ばかりに.

items.q: 準備しなかった___、失敗しました。
items.en: Simply because I hadn't prepared, I failed.
items.why: The avoidable small cause takes the outsized fall.

items.q: サインを忘れた___、書類が戻ってきました。
items.en: Just because I forgot to sign, the documents came back.
items.why: One missed signature, one returned application — the pattern's home ground.

items.q: 早く出た___、間に合いました。
items.en: Because I left early — and I'm glad I did — I made it.
items.why: Good outcome → credit; ばかりに only ever ends badly.

items.q: 道を間違えた___、一時間も遅れました。
items.en: Just because I took a wrong turn, I was a whole hour late.
items.why: Small slip, large delay, audible regret.

drill.note: Four becauses, four temperatures: から asserts, ので presents, おかげで credits, せいで blames — and ばかりに regrets. Read the outcome's temperature before picking.

items.q: 雨の___で、中止です。
items.en: Called off because of the rain — and the rain is blamed.
items.why: Bad outcome, owned and blamed → せいで.

items.q: 晴れた___、できました。
items.en: Because it cleared up — bless the weather — we could do it.
items.why: Credited → おかげで; a bare reason-word would state it without taking a side.

items.q: 寝坊した___、遅刻した。
items.en: Late because of oversleeping — the blame lands.
items.why: Bad result, blamed cause.

items.q: 一言言わなかった___、大きな問題になった。
items.en: Just because one word went unsaid — a real problem.
items.why: The SMALL avoidable cause with the LARGE result is ばかりに's exclusive claim; せいで blames without the smallness.

items.q: ミスをした。でも、人の___にしなかった。
items.en: He made the mistake — but didn't pin it on anyone.
items.why: せいにする — the blame verb, declined.

seg: this problem — about to become subject matter
THE POINT — 'about': names the topic and holds it out as the object of discussion
nitsuite.note: は sets a topic you then talk around; について holds the noun out in front of the sentence as the thing under discussion. First of the family that turns nouns into subject matter.

wr.t: Before a noun it needs の: 問題についての説明. Without の, について modifies the verb; with の it modifies the noun — the same rule every compound particle in this step follows.
wr.jp: 日本の社会についての本を読みました。
wr.en: I read a book about Japanese society.

items.q: この問題___話しましょう。
items.en: Let's talk about this problem.
items.why: Subject matter, held out for discussion → について.

items.q: 日本の社会___の本を読みました。
items.en: I read a book about Japanese society.
items.why: A book ABOUT a topic — and before the noun 本, it takes の.

items.q: 質問___、はっきり答えました。
items.en: I answered the question clearly — facing it.
items.why: The question is confronted, not discussed → に対して.

items.q: 私___、この経験は大切です。
items.en: For me, this experience matters.
items.why: A viewpoint with an evaluation after it → にとって.

items.q: 将来___、家族と話しました。
items.en: I talked with my family about the future.
items.why: The future is the subject matter of the talk.

seg: THE POINT — 'toward': points the attitude at what it faces
nitaishite.note: について is about; に対して is toward — the noun is being confronted or responded to, not discussed. Ask whether the noun is a subject or a target.

wr.t: に対して also draws formal contrasts between two things: 〜のに対して, 'whereas'. The facing becomes a face-off between clauses.
wr.jp: 兄が静かなのに対して、弟はにぎやかです。
wr.en: Whereas the older brother is quiet, the younger is lively.

items.q: 質問___、はっきり答えました。
items.en: I answered the question clearly.
items.why: The answer faces the question → に対して.

items.q: 彼は学生___とても厳しいです。
items.en: He is very strict toward his students.
items.why: An attitude aimed at a target.

items.q: この問題___話しましょう。
items.en: Let's talk about this problem.
items.why: Discussed, not confronted → について.

items.q: お客様___、ていねいに話してください。
items.en: Please speak politely toward customers.
items.why: Conduct aimed at people → に対して.

items.q: 兄が静かな___、弟はにぎやかです。
items.en: Whereas the older brother is quiet, the younger is lively.
items.why: The formal whereas — two clauses face off.

seg: THE POINT — 'depending on': as this changes, so does that
niyotte.note: The widest of the family: by means of (method), by (the doer, in a passive), depending on (it varies). Three jobs, one shape — context alone separates them.

wr.t: In a passive sentence によって marks the doer at document height — the register where 〜に would be too light for the deed.
wr.jp: この歌は有名な人によって作られました。
wr.en: This song was written by someone famous.

items.q: 人___、意見が違います。
items.en: Opinions differ from person to person.
items.why: The depending-on job: person varies, opinion varies with it.

items.q: この方法___、問題が解決しました。
items.en: The problem was solved by this method.
items.why: By means of — the method job.

items.q: この歌は有名な人___作られました。
items.en: This song was written by someone famous.
items.why: The doer of a passive, formally → によって.

items.q: 国___、あいさつの仕方が違います。
items.en: Greetings differ by country.
items.why: Country is the variable; the custom rides it.

items.q: 天気___、行くかどうか決めます。
items.en: We'll decide depending on the weather.
items.why: The decision hangs on the variable.

seg: THE POINT — で in a suit: place, time or field, at document height
was discussed — passive, matching the register
nioite.note: It says nothing で could not say; what it adds is the register of the room it is said in — documents, ceremonies, academic writing.

wr.t: Before a noun it becomes における — the arena worn as a title. Stage 12 builds a whole lesson on that form; meet the seam here.
wr.jp: 日本における環境の問題は大きいです。
wr.en: Environmental issues in Japan are serious.

items.q: 会議___、その問題が話し合われました。
items.en: The matter was discussed at the meeting.
items.why: The formal stage for the event → において.

items.q: 日本___環境の問題
items.en: Environmental issues in Japan (as a title would print it)
items.why: Before a noun the formal stage takes its の-form: における.

items.q: 式は体育館___行われます。
items.en: The ceremony will be held in the gymnasium.
items.why: Ceremony + formal register → において where plain で would also do.

items.q: 私___、この経験は大切です。
items.en: For me, this experience matters.
items.why: A viewpoint, not a venue.

items.q: 現代___、スマホは生活の一部です。
items.en: In the modern age, phones are part of life.
items.why: A time as formal stage — において covers eras as well as rooms.

seg: me — the holder of the viewpoint
THE POINT — 'for / as far as X is concerned': the judgement's vantage
matters a great deal — an evaluation, as にとって demands
nitotte.note: What follows にとって is almost always an evaluation — important, difficult, precious. It is not the 'for' of gifts or purposes; it is the 'for' of verdicts.

wr.t: For gifts and purposes, plain に or のために does the job — 母にプレゼントを買った. にとって there would claim a viewpoint where only a recipient exists.
wr.jp: 母にプレゼントを買いました。
wr.en: I bought a present for my mother — plain に, not にとって.

items.q: 私___、この経験はとても大切です。
items.en: For me, this experience matters a great deal.
items.why: Viewpoint + evaluation → にとって.

items.q: 学生___、その本は少し難しいです。
items.en: For students, that book is a little difficult.
items.why: Difficulty judged from the students' vantage.

items.q: 母___プレゼントを買いました。
items.en: I bought a present for my mother.
items.why: A recipient, not a viewpoint — plain に.

items.q: 外国人___、敬語は難しいです。
items.en: For foreigners, keigo is hard.
items.why: The verdict 'hard' is issued from a named vantage.

items.q: この写真は、私___宝物です。
items.en: To me, this photo is a treasure.
items.why: 宝物 is an evaluation — the vantage owns it.

drill.note: Five に-compounds, one map: について subject matter, に対して the faced target, によって the variable/means/doer, において the formal stage, にとって the viewpoint. English flattens four of them to 'about' or 'for' — the drill is the map.

items.q: 問題___話す
items.en: Discuss the problem — subject matter.
items.why: Held out and discussed → について.

items.q: 質問___答える
items.en: Answer the question — facing it.
items.why: The response aims at its target.

items.q: 人___違う
items.en: Differs from person to person.
items.why: The variable job.

items.q: 会議___話し合う
items.en: Discuss at the meeting — the formal stage.
items.why: The venue in a suit.

items.q: 私___大切だ
items.en: Important to me — my viewpoint.
items.why: Vantage plus evaluation.

seg: 電車が止まっていたんです。
the trains were stopped — the reason, just learned
THE POINT — the conclusion clicking into place: 'that's why'
wakeda.note: Not a reason — a conclusion drawn FROM a reason already on the table. The sound of something clicking: no wonder, that explains it, so that's why.

wr.t: 道理で pairs with it naturally: 道理で〜わけだ — 'no wonder'. The click, doubled: the listener announces that the world just made sense.
wr.jp: 十年住んでいるんですか。道理で日本語が上手なわけですね。
wr.en: Ten years? No wonder your Japanese is good.

items.q: 十年住んでいるんですか。道理で上手な___ですね。
items.en: Ten years? No wonder you're good.
items.why: The reason is known; the conclusion clicks → わけ.

items.q: 電車が止まっていたんです。だから遅れた___です。
items.en: The trains were stopped — so that's why I was late.
items.why: Conclusion drawn from the fact just given.

items.q: 寒い___だ。雪が降っている。
items.en: No wonder it's cold — look, snow.
items.why: The evidence is in view; the click follows.

items.q: 切符を買ったから、来る___です。
items.en: He bought a ticket, so he should be coming.
items.why: Expectation with receipts, BEFORE the outcome — はず, not the click of わけ.

items.q: 彼は毎日練習している。上手になる___だ。
items.en: He practices daily — naturally he's improving.
items.why: The known habit explains the observed skill.

seg: that I dislike it — the conclusion you were about to draw
THE POINT — 'it doesn't follow': the inference denied, not the fact
I just don't eat much of it
wakedewanai.note: The careful denial: not 'it isn't so' but 'it doesn't follow'. The fact stands; the conclusion the listener was reaching for is turned away.

wr.t: With 全部 or みんな it becomes partial denial — not ALL of it — the polite escape from a totalizing question.
wr.jp: 全部わかったわけではありません。
wr.en: It's not that I understood all of it.

items.q: 嫌いな___ではありませんが、あまり食べません。
items.en: It's not that I dislike it — I just don't eat much.
items.why: Denying the inference the listener drew → わけではない.

items.q: 全部わかった___ではありません。
items.en: It's not that I understood all of it.
items.why: Partial denial — the total conclusion refused.

items.q: 高い___ではないが、安くもない。
items.en: Not that it's expensive — but it's not cheap either.
items.why: Both edges denied; the middle held.

items.q: 行きたくない___ではありません。時間がないんです。
items.en: It's not that I don't want to go — there's just no time.
items.why: The unkind inference (you don't want to) is what gets denied.

items.q: 日本人がみんな敬語が上手な___ではない。
items.en: It's not that all Japanese people are good at keigo.
items.why: The generalization is the thing refused.

seg: say — dictionary form, always, before べき
THE POINT — 'ought to have': judgement with no rulebook behind it, and でした closes it over a road not taken
beki.note: なければなりません has a source — a rule, a deadline. べき has only judgement: this is right, and I say so. English 'should' covers both; Japanese does not.

wr.t: The negative attaches to べき, never to the verb: 言うべきではない — 'shouldn't say'. 言わないべき does not exist.
wr.jp: そんなことを言うべきではありません。
wr.en: You shouldn't say things like that.

items.q: もっと早く言う___でした。
items.en: I should have said something sooner.
items.why: Moral judgement over a road not taken → べきでした.

items.q: そんなことを言う___ではありません。
items.en: You shouldn't say things like that.
items.why: The negative rides べき itself.

items.q: 学生はもっと本を読む___だ。
items.en: Students ought to read more.
items.why: An ought issued on the speaker's own judgement.

items.q: 約束は守る___です。
items.en: Promises ought to be kept.
items.why: No rulebook needed — the judgement is the source.

items.q: 疲れているなら、早く帰って休む___だよ。
items.en: If you're that tired, you ought to go home and rest.
items.why: Advice as moral should.

seg: the lights are off — the evidence
THE POINT — 'must have': the strongest guess the language has that is still a guess
nichigainai.note: The top of the certainty dial built since Step 7: でしょう leans, かもしれない allows, はず expects with receipts — に違いない concludes and leaves no room.

wr.t: Polite: に違いありません. And a signpost ahead: Stage 12 promotes this to paper as に相違ない — same height, harder collar. Recognize the family when it arrives.
wr.jp: この字は先生のに違いありません。
wr.en: This handwriting must be the teacher's.

items.q: 電気が消えている。もう帰った___。
items.en: The lights are off — he must have gone home.
items.why: The evidence closes it — the dial's top stop.

items.q: この字は先生の___ありません。
items.en: This handwriting must be the teacher's.
items.why: に違いありません — the polite form of the certainty.

items.q: かばんがない。教室に忘れた___。
items.en: My bag's gone — I must have left it in the classroom.
items.why: Conclusion from the missing bag.

items.q: 三日も寝ていないんだから、疲れている___。
items.en: Three days without sleep — he has to be exhausted.
items.why: The evidence is stated; the conclusion admits no room.

items.q: 空が暗い。雨が降る___。
items.en: The sky is dark — it's bound to rain.
items.why: Read the sky, close the guess.

seg: when you're young — the general case, not this case
THE POINT — the general truth: that's how the world goes, and everybody knows it
monoda.note: A claim about how the world works, not about this instance — with a faint weight of common sense: you are being gently reminded of what everyone knows.

wr.t: After た it turns nostalgic: used to — the general truth of a past era, fondly held.
wr.jp: 学生の頃は、よく遊んだものです。
wr.en: Back in my student days, we used to go out a lot.

items.q: 若い時は、失敗する___です。
items.en: When you're young, you make mistakes — that's how it goes.
items.why: The world's way, stated as common sense → ものだ.

items.q: 学生の頃は、よく遊んだ___です。
items.en: Back in my student days, we used to go out a lot.
items.why: た + ものだ — the nostalgic used-to.

items.q: 人の話は、最後まで聞く___だ。
items.en: One listens to people to the end — that's how it's done.
items.why: The gentle normative flavor of ものだ.

items.q: 時間がたつのは早い___ですね。
items.en: How time flies — doesn't it just.
items.why: A general truth, sighed.

items.q: 昔はこの町も静かだった___です。
items.en: This town used to be quiet, back in the day.
items.why: Nostalgia over an era, not a report on a date.

drill.note: The certainty dial, one line at last: でしょう (probably) → かもしれない (maybe) → はず (expected, with receipts) → に違いない (concluded, from evidence) — and わけだ, the click when a KNOWN reason explains what you see. Read the evidence, pick the stop.

items.q: 明日は雨___。
items.en: It'll probably rain tomorrow — the forecast's word.
items.why: Leaning probable, no evidence in hand → でしょう.

items.q: 雨が降る___。
items.en: It might rain — an honest coin-flip.
items.why: Genuine maybe → かもしれない.

items.q: 切符を買ったから、来る___です。
items.en: He bought a ticket — he should be coming.
items.why: Expectation with receipts → はず.

items.q: 電気が消えている。帰った___。
items.en: Lights off — he must have gone home.
items.why: The evidence closes it → the top stop.

items.q: 十年住んでいるから、上手な___だ。
items.en: Ten years here — no wonder he's good.
items.why: The reason is already known; this is the click, not a guess.

seg: the ます-stem of 降る — the mounting point for the whole family
THE POINT — bolted onto the stem: supplies the beginning the verb didn't have
hajimeru.note: The family's door: take a stem, bolt a second verb on, and the second one adds a shape — here, a beginning. Learn the socket once and five endings share it.

wr.t: The stem is the same socket for every ending in this step — 読みはじめる, 食べおわる, 言いかける, 走りぬく. One mounting point, five machines.
wr.jp: 八時に読みはじめました。
wr.en: I started reading at eight.

items.q: 雨が降り___ました。
items.en: It started raining.
items.why: A beginning bolted onto 降り.

items.q: 八時に読み___ました。
items.en: I started reading at eight.
items.why: The reading opened at eight.

items.q: 赤ちゃんが歩き___ました。
items.en: The baby started walking.
items.why: A first beginning if ever there was one.

items.q: この本を読み___ました。
items.en: I finished reading this book.
items.why: Finished, not begun — the other end of the machine.

items.q: ベルが鳴って、みんな書き___ました。
items.en: The bell rang and everyone started writing.
items.why: The bell opens the writing.

seg: THE POINT — closes the action; たら waits on the closing
owaru.note: The clean close, pairing with はじめる so neatly the two are learned in one breath. The action ends; nothing is said about effort or attitude — that's ぬく and っぱなし's business.

wr.t: For a deliberate, formal close 終える steps in: レポートを書き終えた — the completion owned as an act rather than merely reached.
wr.jp: レポートをやっと書きおわりました。
wr.en: I finally finished writing the report.

items.q: この本を読み___ました。
items.en: I've finished reading this book.
items.why: The reading closed.

items.q: ___たら、行きましょう。
items.en: Let's go once we've finished eating.
items.why: たら waits on the finished eating.

items.q: レポートを書き___ました。
items.en: I finally finished writing the report.
items.why: The long write, closed.

items.q: 映画を見___ってから、寝ました。
items.en: I went to bed after finishing the film.
items.why: 見おわってから — the close, then the bed.

items.q: 雨が降り___ました。
items.en: It started raining.
items.why: A beginning — the pair's other half.

seg: THE POINT — begun and not finished: the half-read state, in one word
linking の — the state worn by a noun
three of them — the counter for bound things
kakeru.note: The no-English-equivalent one: begun and abandoned mid-arc. かけの before a noun is the half-X; 言いかけて is the sentence started and dropped.

wr.t: かける has a darker second job: 'came close to' — 死にかけた, nearly died. Context separates the half-done from the almost-happened.
wr.jp: 何か言いかけて、やめました。
wr.en: He started to say something, then stopped.

items.q: 読み___の本が三冊あります。
items.en: I've got three books on the go.
items.why: Half-read — begun, not finished.

items.q: 何か言い___て、やめました。
items.en: He started to say something, then stopped.
items.why: The sentence begun and dropped mid-air.

items.q: 飲み___のコーヒーが机にあります。
items.en: There's a half-drunk coffee on the desk.
items.why: The abandoned-midway state, worn by the coffee.

items.q: 手紙を書き___のまま、寝てしまいました。
items.en: I fell asleep with the letter half-written.
items.why: Half-written, and left that way.

items.q: 最後まで走り___ました。
items.en: I ran it all the way to the end.
items.why: Carried through — the mirror of かける.

seg: THE POINT — carried all the way through, against resistance: the pride is inside the verb
nuku.note: Not mere completion — completion that took something. The difference between 走りおわった (the run ended) and 走りぬいた (I saw it through).

wr.t: The three you will actually meet: やりぬく, 考えぬく, 走りぬく — do it through, think it through, run it through. Each says the finishing cost something.
wr.jp: よく考えぬいて決めました。
wr.en: I thought it through properly before deciding.

items.q: 最後まで走り___ました。
items.en: I ran it all the way to the end.
items.why: Completion against difficulty — the pride verb.

items.q: よく考え___て決めました。
items.en: I thought it through properly before deciding.
items.why: 考えぬく — thought carried all the way.

items.q: 難しかったですが、最後までやり___ました。
items.en: It was hard, but I saw it through.
items.why: やりぬく — finished, and it cost something.

items.q: マラソンを走り___のは大変でした。
items.en: Running the marathon all the way through was tough.
items.why: The dictionary form of the carry-through.

items.q: 読み___の本
items.en: A half-read book.
items.why: Half-done is かけ; ぬき would claim a finish.

seg: THE POINT — left that way, and it shouldn't have been: the criticism is the meaning
ppanashi.note: A compound with an attitude: the state was left unattended, and the word itself disapproves. No tone of voice required.

wr.t: The base is 放す, to release: the thing was released from care and stayed that way. Lights, windows, taps — the pattern's home turf, and っぱなしにする is the act of leaving it so.
wr.jp: 窓を開けっぱなしにしないでください。
wr.en: Please don't leave the window open.

items.q: 電気がつけ___でした。
items.en: The light had been left on.
items.why: Left on, and shouldn't have been — the criticism is in the word.

items.q: 窓を開け___にしないでください。
items.en: Please don't leave the window open.
items.why: っぱなしにする — the act of leaving-so, forbidden.

items.q: 水が出___ですよ。
items.en: The tap's been left running, you know.
items.why: Running unattended — the word tuts for you.

items.q: テレビをつけ___で寝てしまいました。
items.en: I fell asleep with the TV left on.
items.why: The state left uncared-for while you slept.

items.q: ドアを開け___にしたのは誰ですか。
items.en: Who left the door standing open?
items.why: The accusation the suffix was built for.

drill.note: One stem, five endings, two axes: how far the action got (はじめる → かける → おわる → ぬく) and what you think of the state it was left in (っぱなし). The drill is the axis.

items.q: 半分だけ読んだ本 → 読み___の本
items.en: A book half-read → the half-read book.
items.why: Begun, not finished → かけ.

items.q: 大変だったが、最後までやり___た。
items.en: It was hard, but I saw it through.
items.why: Completion that cost something → ぬく; おわる would report the end without the fight.

items.q: たった今、雨が降り___ました。
items.en: It's just started raining.
items.why: A beginning, freshly opened.

items.q: 電気を消すのを忘れた → つけ___
items.en: Forgot to switch it off → left on.
items.why: The unattended state, with the built-in reproach.

items.q: 全部読んだ → 読み___た。
items.en: Read it all → finished reading.
items.why: A plain clean close — no struggle claimed, so not ぬく.

seg: THE POINT — prone to: a pattern, not an event, and an unwelcome one
gachi.note: The difference between 'I was ill' and 'I get ill a lot' — the second claims a pattern, and がち claims it with a frown. Welcome tendencies don't take がち.

wr.t: It attaches to nouns as well as stems: 病気がち, 留守がち — the tendency named without a verb in sight.
wr.jp: 子どもの頃は病気がちでした。
wr.en: I was often ill as a child.

items.q: 最近、忘れ___です。
items.en: I've been forgetful lately.
items.why: A recurring unwelcome pattern → がち.

items.q: 子どもの頃は病気___でした。
items.en: I was often ill as a child.
items.why: The noun-mounted tendency.

items.q: 冬は家にいる___になります。
items.en: In winter I tend to stay in.
items.why: A seasonal pattern, mildly rued.

items.q: ちょっと風邪___です。
items.en: I've got a touch of a cold coming on.
items.why: A slight lean toward the state, not a recurring pattern → 気味.

items.q: 曇り___の天気が続きます。
items.en: The weather will stay mostly cloudy.
items.why: 曇りがち — the forecast's own tendency word.

seg: a cold — the state being leaned toward
THE POINT — a touch of: the shadow of the state, not the state itself
gimi.note: がち counts occurrences; 気味 measures a lean. 風邪気味 is not a cold — it is a cold's shadow falling across you.

wr.t: Attached, it reads ぎみ: 疲れぎみ. Standing alone, 気味 lives in 気味が悪い — 'creepy' — a different animal wearing the same characters.
wr.jp: 最近、疲れ気味です。
wr.en: I've been a touch tired lately.

items.q: ちょっと風邪___です。
items.en: I've got a bit of a cold coming on.
items.why: The shadow of the state → 気味.

items.q: 最近、疲れ___です。
items.en: I've been a touch tired lately.
items.why: A lean, not a count of episodes.

items.q: 最近、忘れ___です。
items.en: I've been forgetful lately — it keeps happening.
items.why: Recurring events → がち; 気味 would claim only a faint lean.

items.q: 少し太り___なので、歩いています。
items.en: I'm getting a touch heavy, so I've been walking.
items.why: The gentle lean toward a state.

items.q: 電車は遅れ___です。
items.en: The trains tend to run late.
items.why: A pattern of episodes → がち.

seg: the price — the benchmark about to be set
THE POINT — 'for a': the expectation the benchmark set, undercut
it's good — surprisingly, and the surprise is the point
warini.note: Sets an expectation and then beats it (or falls short of it). English does this with 'for' and a raised eyebrow; Japanese puts the eyebrow in the particle.

wr.t: Verbs and adjectives connect directly, no の: 若いわりに, 勉強しないわりに — any expectation-bearing thing can be the benchmark.
wr.jp: 彼は若いわりに、しっかりしています。
wr.en: For someone so young, he's very together.

items.q: 値段の___、おいしいです。
items.en: For the price, it's good.
items.why: The price set an expectation; the taste beat it.

items.q: 若い___、しっかりしています。
items.en: For someone so young, he's very together — said admiringly.
items.why: わりに admires the gap; くせに would sneer at it. Same gap, opposite temperature.

items.q: 勉強しない___、成績がいいです。
items.en: For someone who doesn't study, his grades are good.
items.why: Expectation undercut, eyebrow raised.

items.q: この店は有名な___、安いです。
items.en: For such a famous place, it's cheap.
items.why: Fame predicted expensive; the bill disagreed.

items.q: たくさん練習した___、上手になりませんでした。
items.en: For all that practice, I didn't improve.
items.why: The benchmark can be beaten downward too.

seg: if you practice — the ば form opens the frame
do — repeated: the part that feels strange for a week and then stops
THE POINT — 'the more': scales the second thing to the first
bahodo.note: One thing scaled against another, and both languages repeat the verb to do it. ば opens, the repetition holds, ほど scales.

wr.t: Adjectives run the same frame: 安ければ安いほどいい — the cheaper the better. The repetition rule survives the change of part of speech.
wr.jp: 安ければ安いほど、うれしいです。
wr.en: The cheaper, the happier.

items.q: 練習すればする___、上手になります。
items.en: The more you practise, the better you get.
items.why: The scaling frame closes on ほど.

items.q: 考えれば考える___、わからなくなります。
items.en: The more I think, the less I understand.
items.why: Scaled downward — the frame doesn't care which way.

items.q: 安ければ安い___、うれしいです。
items.en: The cheaper, the happier.
items.why: Adjectives run the same machine.

items.q: 練習___するほど、上手になります。
items.en: The more you practise, the better you get.
items.why: The ば form is what opens the frame — no other conditional does.

items.q: 日本語は、使えば使う___上手になります。
items.en: Japanese improves the more you use it.
items.why: Use scales skill — the course's own thesis, in the course's own frame.

seg: THE POINT — 'far from': the assumption overturned into its opposite
it was very expensive — the opposite, stated with force
dokoroka.note: A correction with force behind it: not only is it not that — it is the reverse. The strongest overturn in the degree family.

wr.t: It escalates as well as reverses: 休むどころか、もっと忙しくなった — never mind X, things went further the other way. The force is the same; the direction is context's.
wr.jp: 休むどころか、もっと忙しくなりました。
wr.en: Far from resting, I got busier.

items.q: 安い___、とても高かったです。
items.en: Far from cheap — it was very expensive.
items.why: The assumption overturned into its opposite.

items.q: 休む___、もっと忙しくなりました。
items.en: Far from resting, I got busier.
items.why: The hoped-for rest reversed with force.

items.q: 雨は止む___、強くなりました。
items.en: Far from stopping, the rain got heavier.
items.why: The overturn, weather edition.

items.q: 彼は英語___、中国語も話せます。
items.en: Never mind English — he speaks Chinese too.
items.why: The escalating reading: the lesser case waved aside.

items.q: 値段の___、おいしいです。
items.en: For the price, it's good.
items.why: An expectation UNDERCUT is わりに; どころか needs a full reversal.

drill.note: The graders on one bench: がち (often, unwelcome), 気味 (a touch), わりに (against the benchmark), ば〜ほど (scaled), どころか (overturned). Read the claim's temperature, then pick.

items.q: 最近、忘れ___だ。
items.en: I keep forgetting things lately.
items.why: A pattern of episodes → がち.

items.q: ちょっと疲れ___だ。
items.en: A touch tired.
items.why: A lean, not a count → 気味.

items.q: 値段の___、おいしい。
items.en: Good, for the price.
items.why: Benchmark set, expectation beaten.

items.q: 安い___、高かった。
items.en: Far from cheap — expensive.
items.why: Full reversal → どころか; わりに only bends expectations.

items.q: 練習すればする___うまくなる。
items.en: The more you practise, the better you get.
items.why: The scaling frame.

seg: THE POINT — 'exactly as': matching, not roughly like
toori.note: The claim is precision: as said, as written, as planned — no deviation. Roughly-like is ように's territory; とおり matches.

wr.t: After a noun it voices to どおり: 予定どおり, 時間どおり — the same precision, compounded straight onto the noun.
wr.jp: 会議は予定どおり始まりました。
wr.en: The meeting started exactly on schedule.

items.q: 言った___にやりました。
items.en: I did it exactly as you said.
items.why: Matching the specification → とおり.

items.q: 会議は予定___始まりました。
items.en: The meeting started on schedule.
items.why: Noun + どおり — the voiced compound.

items.q: 説明書の___に作ってください。
items.en: Please build it exactly as the manual says.
items.why: Instructions demand matching, not resembling.

items.q: 私が言う___に書いてください。
items.en: Write exactly what I say.
items.why: Dictation — precision by definition.

items.q: 天気予報___、雨が降りました。
items.en: Just as the forecast said, it rained.
items.why: 予報どおり — the forecast matched.

seg: not-knowing — the state he was not in
THE POINT — put the state on: pretending as an action, with its own noun and verb
furi.note: Japanese makes the pretence a noun plus する — which means the pretending is itself the act being reported, not a flavor on another verb.

wr.t: Nouns connect with の: 病気のふりをする. And note the everyday art form 聞こえないふり — the practiced skill of not hearing.
wr.jp: 彼は聞こえないふりをしました。
wr.en: He pretended not to hear.

items.q: 彼は知らない___をしました。
items.en: He pretended not to know.
items.why: A state performed, not held → ふりをする.

items.q: 寝た___をしていました。
items.en: I was pretending to be asleep.
items.why: The put-on sleep.

items.q: 病気の___をして、会社を休みました。
items.en: He faked being ill and skipped work.
items.why: Noun + の + ふり.

items.q: 聞こえない___をしないでください。
items.en: Don't pretend you can't hear me.
items.why: The named art of not-hearing, forbidden.

items.q: 彼女は元気な___をしていましたが、つらそうでした。
items.en: She was putting on a cheerful front, but you could see the strain.
items.why: The front is worn; ふり names the wearing.

seg: THE POINT — 'though it is': the contradiction living inside one body
it's a good shop — the other true thing
nagaramo.note: Step 7's ながら put two actions in one body; ながらも keeps the body and adds the disagreement — both halves true of the same person or thing.

wr.t: 残念ながら is this pattern fossilized into an adverb: 'regrettably' — the concession worn as a set phrase at the head of bad news.
wr.jp: 残念ながら、今日は行けません。
wr.en: Regrettably, I can't make it today.

items.q: 小さい___も、いい店です。
items.en: Small though it is, it's a good shop.
items.why: The concession inside one shop → ながらも.

items.q: 知ってい___も、何も言いませんでした。
items.en: Even knowing, I said nothing.
items.why: Knowing and not-saying, one person.

items.q: 狭い___も、楽しい部屋です。
items.en: Cramped though it is, it's a cheerful room.
items.why: Two true, disagreeing things about one room.

items.q: ___ながら、今日は行けません。
items.en: Regrettably, I can't make it today.
items.why: The fossil phrase — 残念ながら.

items.q: 学生___も、彼はプロのように働きます。
items.en: Student though he is, he works like a professional.
items.why: Respectful concession → ながらも; くせに (with の) would turn it into a complaint.

seg: THE POINT — 'even though', with a sneer: the speaker resents it
教えてくれませんでした。
wouldn't tell me — the resented conduct
kuseni.note: のに with contempt loaded: the other party had no business being that way. Meet it deliberately, deploy it rarely — the rudeness is the semantics, not the delivery.

wr.t: Nouns need の: 子どものくせに. And keep the aim honest — のに states a mismatch; くせに files a complaint about the person. Only one of them can be retracted.
wr.jp: 子どものくせに、生意気です。
wr.en: Cheeky, for a child — and said with contempt.

items.q: 知っている___、教えてくれませんでした。
items.en: He knew perfectly well — and still wouldn't tell me. (resentful)
items.why: The resentment picks くせに; the others don't even parse here.

items.q: 子どもの___、生意気です。
items.en: Cheeky, for a child — with contempt.
items.why: Noun + のくせに — the contemptuous concession.

items.q: 何も知らない___、わかったような顔をします。
items.en: Knows nothing, and puts on that knowing face.
items.why: The complaint about the person, filed in grammar.

items.q: 自分ではやらない___、文句ばかり言います。
items.en: Never does it himself, and complains nonstop.
items.why: The double standard, sneered at.

items.q: 小さい___も、いい店です。
items.en: Small though it is, it's a good shop — said warmly.
items.why: Warmth → ながらも. くせに would insult the shop.

seg: sat down — た form: the first event, just closed
THE POINT — the seam: the instant it closed, and a surprise came through it
the phone rang — the uninvited second event
totan.note: The finest spoken grain of timing: no gap, no warning, and the surprise is part of the meaning. Always た in front.

wr.t: The second half must be something that happened TO you — a surprise, never a plan. For planned sequences, たら or 次第 hold the schedule.
wr.jp: 外に出たとたん、雨が降りはじめました。
wr.en: The moment I stepped outside, it started raining.

items.q: 座った___、電話が鳴りました。
items.en: The instant I sat down, the phone rang.
items.why: The seam between two events, with a surprise.

items.q: 外に出た___、雨が降りはじめました。
items.en: The moment I stepped outside, it started raining.
items.why: No gap, no warning — とたん.

items.q: 会議の___に、電話が鳴りました。
items.en: The phone rang right in the middle of the meeting.
items.why: Mid-flow, interrupted → 最中; とたん needs a seam.

items.q: 決まり___、ご連絡します。
items.en: I'll contact you as soon as it's decided.
items.why: A promise about the earliest possible moment → 次第.

items.q: ドアを開けた___、猫が出て行きました。
items.en: The moment I opened the door, the cat was out.
items.why: The seam again — and the cat through it.

seg: THE POINT — in the very thick of it: fully underway, and interrupted
the phone rang — at the worst moment, as usual
saichuu.note: Not 'during' in general — right in the thick of it, usually at the worst possible point. Nouns take の最中に; verbs take ている最中に.

wr.t: Verbs must be mid-flow: 話している最中に — the ている is what puts the activity visibly underway for 最中 to interrupt.
wr.jp: 話している最中に、彼は帰ってしまいました。
wr.en: He left while I was still mid-sentence.

items.q: 会議の___に、電話が鳴りました。
items.en: The phone rang right in the middle of the meeting.
items.why: The thick of it, interrupted.

items.q: 話している___に、帰ってしまいました。
items.en: He left while I was still talking.
items.why: ている + 最中 — mid-flow.

items.q: 食事の___に、電話をかけないでください。
items.en: Please don't call during meals — right in the middle of them.
items.why: The interruption pattern, forbidden in advance.

items.q: 座った___、電話が鳴りました。
items.en: The instant I sat down, the phone rang.
items.why: A seam, not a middle → とたん.

items.q: 試合の___に、雨が強くなりました。
items.en: The rain picked up right in the middle of the match.
items.why: Fully underway, then interrupted.

seg: THE POINT — the moment it becomes possible: the business register's as-soon-as
I will contact you — a promise, which is 次第's natural cargo
shidai.note: Forward-looking and controlled: as soon as X is done, I will do Y. Arrangements and promises, not narration — the ご連絡します register.

wr.t: A different 次第 hides in 次第だ after nouns: あなた次第です — it's up to you. Same characters, different machine; meet it now so it doesn't ambush you later.
wr.jp: 行くかどうかは、あなた次第です。
wr.en: Whether we go is up to you.

items.q: 決まり___、ご連絡します。
items.en: I'll be in touch as soon as it's decided.
items.why: The business as-soon-as, with a promise attached.

items.q: 到着___、始めましょう。
items.en: Let's start as soon as everyone's arrived.
items.why: Arrangement grammar — stem + 次第.

items.q: 終わり___、帰ってもいいですよ。
items.en: You may go home as soon as you finish.
items.why: Permission scheduled on completion.

items.q: 行くかどうかは、あなた___です。
items.en: Whether we go is up to you.
items.why: The other 次第 — it-depends-on-you.

items.q: 座った___、電話が鳴りました。
items.en: The instant I sat down, the phone rang.
items.why: A surprise at a seam is とたん; 次第 promises, never surprises.

drill.note: Three grains of when: とたん — the seam, and a surprise; 最中 — the thick of it, interrupted; 次第 — as soon as possible, and a promise. Ask where in the event you are standing.

items.q: 家に着いた___、雨が降りはじめた。
items.en: The moment I got home, it started raining.
items.why: Seam + surprise → とたん.

items.q: 勉強している___に、友だちが来た。
items.en: A friend turned up right while I was studying.
items.why: Mid-flow, interrupted → 最中.

items.q: 準備ができ___、出発します。
items.en: We leave as soon as preparations are done.
items.why: A schedule, promised → 次第.

items.q: 立ち上がった___、頭が痛くなった。
items.en: The instant I stood up, my head hurt.
items.why: The unplanned second event at the seam.

items.q: 会議の___に、スマホが鳴ってしまった。
items.en: My phone went off right in the middle of the meeting.
items.why: The worst possible middle — 最中's specialty.
